target_only_tests.note: Four cases, none counted as ported coverage. Each was measured red under a named mutation and green again on revert (rule 10). TWO SEAM LIVENESS CASES, required because this module carries two seams and a seam nothing routes through keeps every case that replaces it green for the wrong reason. `production reads the clock through its seam` (C1: calling `new Date()` directly turns it red, `expected +0 to be 1`) -- and note this is NOT already covered by the frozen-clock cases: those would fail today only because the frozen instant is months in the past, which is an accident of the calendar rather than an assertion. `production sleeps through its seam` (C2: moving the sleep above the iteration check turns it red, `expected [10, 10] to deeply equal [10]`) -- it also pins that the loop does NOT sleep after its last iteration, which is the difference between `--max-iterations 2` returning at once and returning ten seconds late for anyone who scripts around it. ONE CASE FOR THE PORT'S OWN PROCESS TOP LEVEL. `a refusal from a command becomes an exit code, not a stack trace` (C3: removing `main`'s `ArgparseExit` catch turns it red). In Python a `SystemExit` escaping `main` is what sets the process's exit status, and the interpreter's own top level does that; Node has no such top level, so without the catch the refusal `loadCfgOrExit` carefully wrote would reach the operator buried under an unhandled error. The source needs no case for this because CPython supplies the behaviour. ONE MOUNT CASE. `attention is mounted on the unified parser` (C4: removing the mount turns it red) pins the D-0030 arrangement the whole file rests on -- every ported case above parses through the shipped `continuo` parser, so if the mount or a flag's `dest` were wrong they would all fail at once and none of them would say why. This one says why.

notes: `approved_non_running` is empty because the file uses no non-running construct. Checked directly against scripts/parity-check.mjs's own NON_RUNNING patterns -- `(test|it|describe).skip`, `(test|it|describe).todo`, `(test|it).fails`, `skipIf(` and `xfail(` -- over test/attention/cli.test.ts with comments and string literals INCLUDED, which is stricter than the sweep: no match. `conditionally_collected` is empty for the same reason: nothing here is absent from a host's collection, and all 26 mapped ids plus the 4 target-only ones were present in `vitest list --json` when this ledger was written (30 collected from this file, 30 passed).

THE RULE 9 ANSWERS. (1) WHICH CALLER-SUPPLIED STRINGS ARE USED AS A MAP KEY: the payload keys this module writes onto `event.to_dict()`'s result -- `title`, `body`, `desktop_dispatched`, `bell_dispatched`, `delivered` -- are literals of this module's own, not caller-supplied, and the object they are written onto is built by `AttentionEvent.toDict()`. The caller-supplied keys of the pipeline (the attention kind, the dedup key) are read inside `classifier.ts`, `config.ts` and `dedup.ts`, each of which guards them and each of which has its own ledger entry saying so. (2) WHICH `number` PARAMETERS THE SOURCE TYPES `int`: `poll_interval_sec`, through `max(1, int(cfg.poll_interval_sec))`. A2's loader already refuses a non-integer for it, and `Math.trunc` reproduces `int()`'s truncation-toward-zero for the value that does arrive. `max_iterations` is `type=int` on the parser, which is the port's own argparse transcription and converts before `choices`, exactly as `_get_values` does. The two epoch numbers (`now.timestamp()`) are floats on both sides.

WHAT `pyJsonDumps` BUYS OVER `JSON.stringify` FOR THE `--json` PAYLOAD. The payload carries an operator's template text, and `json.dump(..., ensure_ascii=False)` and `JSON.stringify` disagree about a lone surrogate: `JSON.stringify` emits a `\udXXX` escape where CPython's encoder raises, and about non-BMP characters they agree only because both emit them raw. The module reuses the port's existing CPython `json.dumps` transcription rather than growing a second local rendering of the same function, which is the rule-11 argument A2 makes for `pytime.ts`. `indent=2` and the trailing newline are the source's.

ONE DIVERGENCE THAT IS NOT REPRODUCED, and it is a mechanism rather than a behaviour. `cmd_attention_watch` wraps its loop in `except KeyboardInterrupt` and prints one line. There is nothing to catch here: Node delivers SIGINT as a process signal rather than as an exception raised inside the loop, so an equivalent would have to install a handler on `process` -- a different mechanism, with a lifetime that outlives the function that installed it. No source case exercises the branch (there is no way to raise `KeyboardInterrupt` inside `time.sleep` from a test without patching the sleep to raise, which the source does not do), so nothing is lost from the evidence set; it is recorded here rather than left for a reader to notice the missing `try`.

WHY THE PORT'S `scan` CAN EXIT NON-ZERO WHERE THE SOURCE'S ALWAYS RETURNED 0 ON A BROKEN LEDGER: D-0951. The source has exactly one `SystemExit` in this module, for an unreadable config, and recovers silently from a corrupt dedup file. A2's D-0904 removed the recovery; the CLI's answer to the refusal is A3's decision and is the entry's subject. The exit code is 2, the same the config refusal uses, because both mean an input this command was pointed at cannot be used.

entries.target_id: test/attention/cli.test.ts::attention cli > a broken dedup ledger is refused, not recovered
entries.reason: ADAPTED, AND THIS IS THE BELT'S REPAIRED DEFECT rather than a mechanical rewrite. THE SOURCE ASSERTS: a `{ broken` dedup file makes `attention scan` return 0, and the file is valid JSON afterwards -- i.e. the corrupt ledger is silently replaced with an empty one. parity/source-inventory.belts.md names that behaviour as ruled out for durable dedup state and D-0034 ratified the repair; A2's D-0904 made `loadState` fail closed, because an empty ledger says nothing has been notified and therefore frees every already-handled event to fire again -- the resume-without-double-execution violation D-0001 exists to prevent. The third assertion is the one the source's version destroys and is not merely the negation of it. What A2's decision did NOT settle is what the CLI does with the refusal; that is A3's call and is recorded in D-0951. Probe C5: swallowing `DedupStateRefused` and returning 0 -- the source's behaviour -- turns this red with `expected the command to exit, and it returned`.
